author: Brünnich, 1764
habitat: 바닷가나 호숫가의 풀밭, 논, 하천, 습지
summary: 지금까지 국내 기록이 10건이 안 되는 길잃은새로, 바닷가나 호숫가의 풀밭, 논, 하천, 습지에서 지낸다. 대개 홀로 지내며 밤에만 움직인다. 곤충과 환형동물, 작은 물고기, 게, 새우 등을 잡아먹는다. 구북구 한대와 시베리아에서 번식하며 알 4개를 암컷 혼자 품고, 동남아시아, 남유럽, 아프리카에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Jack Snipe (Lymnocryptes minimus), adult, sexes alike, in autumn as on passage through Korea: crown blackish from the forehead to the nape with no pale central stripe; a split pale buff supercilium, its two pale lines separated by a thin dark line above the eye; a dark eye-stripe and a dark crescent across the lower cheek; chin and throat white; neck sides and breast pale buff, densely streaked and blotched blackish-brown; mantle and scapulars blackish with a purple and green gloss, with two broad straw-buff stripes running down each side of the back; wing coverts dark brown fringed buff; flanks streaked brown; belly and undertail coverts white; tail dark brown, pointed and wedge-shaped, with no orange band. Bill pale yellowish-brown at the base, darker towards the tip; dark eye; legs dull greenish-yellow.
art.pose: crouched alone in wet grass, side view
art.scene: Korean grassy marsh edge beside rice fields during autumn migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing in wet grass: blackish crown band without a pale centre stripe, split buff supercilium, white chin and throat, pale neck sides blotched blackish-brown, glossy purple-green back with two straw-buff stripes, streaked buff breast, white belly and undertail coverts, short straight bill, greenish-yellow legs
adult, head seen obliquely from above: broad blackish central crown band flanked on each side by two pale buff lines, short straight bill
adult, tail spread seen from above: pointed, wedge-shaped tail of 12 dark brown feathers, the central pair longest, with no orange band
art.build: Small, compact snipe, clearly smaller than Common Snipe and about the size of a Dunlin; plump body, short neck and large head with the eye set high and well back. Bill straight, about one and a half times the length of the head, proportionally much shorter than any other snipe's. Legs short, greenish-yellow. The long tertials cover the folded primaries; tail short and pointed. Feeds with a constant rhythmic bobbing of the whole body; flushes silently at very close range and drops back into cover after a short, low flight.
avoid: Do not paint a pale central crown stripe; Common, Pintail and Swinhoe's Snipe have one, but the Jack Snipe's crown centre is all dark.
Do not give it a bill twice the head length (Common Snipe); the Jack Snipe's bill is short for a snipe.
Do not show a rufous-orange band or white corners in the tail; the tail is plain dark and pointed.
Do not paint the back plain brown; it has an iridescent purple-green sheen and bold straw-buff stripes.
